question: Which of the following metals is characterised by low density and softness?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Potassium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potassium** (chemical symbol **K**, from Neo-Latin kalium) is a chemical element with **Atomic Number 19**. It is a silvery-white metal that is **soft** enough to be easily cut with a **knife** with little force.
 
• It is characterized by an extremely **low density** of approximately **0.862 g/cm³** at **20°C**, which is less than that of **water** (1.0 g/cm³). This physical property causes the metal to **float** on the surface of water while it reacts. ***Hence, the correct answer is Potassium.***
 
• As a member of the **Alkali Metals** (Group 1 of the periodic table), it possesses only **one valence electron** in its outer shell. This single electron is involved in **metallic bonding**, which is relatively weak, leading to the characteristic **softness** and **low melting point** (approx **63.5°C**) of the metal.
 
• Due to its extreme **chemical reactivity**, especially with moisture and air, it is never found as a free element in nature and is typically stored under **mineral oil** or **kerosene** to prevent oxidation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Copper (Cu)**:
 
 
• It is a **transition metal** located in **Group 11** of the periodic table.
 
• Unlike potassium, copper has a high density of approximately **8.96 g/cm³** and is significantly harder. It is known for its excellent **electrical conductivity** and **thermal conductivity**. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Aluminium (Al)**:
 
 
• It is a **post-transition metal** in **Group 13**.
 
• While aluminium is known for being **lightweight** compared to steel (density **2.70 g/cm³**), it is much denser than potassium and is a structural metal, not "soft" in the chemical sense of being cut like wax. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Magnesium (Mg)**:
 
 
• It is an **alkaline earth metal** found in **Group 2** of the periodic table with **Atomic Number 12**.
 
• Its density is approximately **1.74 g/cm³**. While it is the lightest structural metal, it is harder than alkali metals like potassium and sodium because it has **two valence electrons**, strengthening its metallic lattice. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Periodic Trends**: In the periodic table, **alkali metals** (Lithium, Sodium, Potassium, Rubidium, Cesium) generally show a decrease in **hardness** and **melting points** as you move down the group due to the increasing **atomic radius** and weakening of metallic bonds.
 
• **Density Comparisons**: Only three metals in the periodic table are light enough to float on water: **Lithium** (lightest solid element), **Sodium**, and **Potassium**.
 
• **Applications**: **Potassium** is vital for biological functions in the human body, specifically for **nerve impulses** and **muscle contractions**. Industrially, it is widely used in the production of **fertilizers** (as potash) and in **specialty glasses**.
 
• **Identification**: Potassium can be identified through a **flame test**, where it emits a characteristic **lilac or light purple** color.
